digests.title: TLDR AI — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Claude Projects v2 💼, Google family agent 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦,

stories.headline: Google wants to give your family its own cloud computer (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's family agent runs on its own cloud computer and Google account, turning the emails, files, and calendars your household shares into daily briefings and updated plans. It can fill out forms and coordinate activities for up to six people, asking permission before acting outside the group. The US experiment has a waitlist.

stories.headline: How Claude is uplifting biomolecular modeling (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Claude enhanced biomolecular modeling by optimizing over 30 models, achieving a 4x speed increase and creating a low-memory mode for predicting larger systems on a single NVIDIA GPU. These improvements, now open-sourced, allow for efficient protein design and structure prediction, potentially accelerating drug discovery. A protein design competition co-sponsored with Adaptyv Bio offers up to $1 million in Claude credits and highlights these advancements.

stories.headline: Projects redesigned: from folder to conversation (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Claude Code Projects let users manage builds by automating task delegation, coordination, and result assembly across cloud sessions. Projects utilize threads for parallel operations, adapting based on progress, and draw on shared memory for efficient task execution. Available now in beta for select subscribers, with wider access coming soon, projects promise enhanced workflow management and context retention.

stories.headline: Noam Brown – Agent swarms, alignment, & recursive self-improvement (72 minute read)
stories.blurb: This post features a transcript of an interview with Noam Brown, a research scientist at OpenAI who works on reasoning, reinforcement learning, self-play, and multi-agent AI. Brown was a foundational contributor to the development of reasoning models. In this interview, Brown talks about multi-agent, Navier-Stokes, the current explosion of maths progress, automating AI research, and how we will know whether models are actually aligned before recursive self-improvement kicks off. A video of the interview is available.

stories.headline: LLM Classification Is Feature Engineering (20 minute read)
stories.blurb: Getting LLMs into shape to reliably serve as classifiers is hard work but potentially highly impactful. More and more research is relying on LLMs for classification, so these tools need to output high-quality results. This post shows how classification is just a feature engineering problem.

stories.headline: Anthropic says its AI now does a quarter of its research work (25 minute read)
stories.blurb: Anthropic says Claude now leads 26% of its AI research work and oversees tens of thousands of active internal agents. Its new measurements track how much AI is helping build the next models, whether people can still oversee those agents, and the computing driving the work.

stories.headline: Toward Recursive Self-Improvement: How GLM Built Its Own Inference Infrastructure (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: Z.ai used a GLM-5.3-powered Infra Agent to help build GLM-5.3-Flash's production serving stack on 100,000+ Chinese accelerators in under two weeks. Dense feedback, kernel fixes, and system-level optimization tripled throughput while keeping humans responsible for objectives and risk.

stories.headline: Introducing Bonsai 2 27B: Near-Lossless Compression in a 9x Smaller Footprint (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Ternary Bonsai 2 27B brings stronger reasoning, coding, vision, and agentic capability to the Bonsai series. It uses ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling, for 1.76 effective bits per weight and a total model footprint of 5.9GB. The model supports a 262K-token context window and multimodal text-and-image input. It can be run on Nvidia GPUs via CUDA and on Apple devices via MLX through custom low-bit kernels.

stories.headline: Helix 2.5 (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Figure introduced Helix 2.5, a humanoid control model pretrained on its Index dataset and tested zero-shot across 30 Bay Area homes. Without collecting training data in those homes, the robots performed tasks including tidying rooms, folding towels, and making beds.

stories.headline: Git as Shared Memory for AI Research Agents (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Agora lets autonomous research agents share findings through an append-only Git DAG, where hypotheses, results, verifications, and reports become reproducible commits.

stories.headline: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash: Omni Senses. Agentic Delivery (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash is a native omnimodal model. It supports a 1M-token context window with text, image, audio, and video inputs. Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash achieves audio-visual performance close to Gemini 3.8 Flash and overall audio performance that exceeds Gemini 3.8 Flash. It is now available on the Qianwen AI Platform.

stories.headline: The Awesome and Alarming AI Visions of Anthropic's CEO (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Dario Amodei, a co-founder and the chief executive of Anthropic, is one of the tech industry's most prolific and polished explainers. He has contributed to dozens of scholarly papers and more recently wrote a half-dozen informal essays for the general public. This article takes a look at his writings to see what they reveal about the AI leader.

stories.headline: Natural General Intelligence (125 minute read)
stories.blurb: AI's potential to transform our relationship with the natural world is often overlooked. Infinite intelligence will not eliminate our need for natural resources. AI promises abundance via the automation of knowledge work, but the Earth system is already fully automated. Natural General Intelligence is a foundation model grounded in the state and dynamics of the planet itself. This article explains the concept, shows readers how it can be built, and explains why it is necessary.

stories.headline: Models know when they're reward hacking — and we can catch them at scale (16 minute read)
stories.blurb: There is a clear internal signal in models that accompanies reward hacking.

stories.headline: Instinct Concierge Can Now Handle Phone Calls (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Instinct is rolling out Concierge, a white-glove service for tasks that require human interaction, including phone calls, high-end bookings, and customer service.

stories.headline: Astra for Law (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Astra for Law is a legal AI foundation that combines GPT-6 Astra with tools, settings, privacy controls, and context designed for professional legal work.

stories.headline: Notion lets teams share the same instructions across AI agents (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Notion's Skills API lets teams edit agent instructions together and distribute them to other agents through GitHub sync or Vercel's skills installer.

digests.title: TLDR IT — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Huawei speeds up AI chips 🧠, OpenAI models evade oversight 👀, Claude Code gets projects 💻

stories.headline: Huawei accelerates next-gen AI chip launch (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Huawei moved up the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip to Q1 2027 as it tries to close the gap with Nvidia. The company says demand for its AI compute hardware in China is already exceeding supply.

stories.headline: Global AI spending projected to hit $2.7T in 2026 (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Gartner expects worldwide AI spending to rise 49.5% this year to $2.7 trillion. The forecast reflects continued spending on AI infrastructure, devices, software, and services as companies move projects into production.

stories.headline: OpenAI discloses concerning behavior from its AI models (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenAI disclosed cases where models tried to evade oversight, conceal mistakes, and work around constraints during testing. It is introducing a framework for systematically tracking and publishing these incidents as increasingly autonomous agents create new monitoring challenges.

stories.headline: Gartner: Why the cloud is holding back agentic AI (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: According to Gartner, traditional centralized cloud architectures are holding back the agentic AI revolution by failing to provide the continuous, high-frequency inference needed for real-time enterprise workflows. Infrastructure and operations leaders need to adopt a hybrid edge-cloud architecture to overcome severe latency barriers, unsustainable hyperscaler bandwidth egress costs, and outage risks.

stories.headline: Microsoft says AI adoption alone won't transform enterprises (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Microsoft says its own AI rollout showed that deploying tools broadly is not enough. Companies need to redesign entire workflows around business outcomes. Proprietary context, evaluations, and organizational learning could become more valuable than access to any individual foundation model.

stories.headline: AI agents are turning retrieval into a major infrastructure problem (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: As agents perform longer tasks, they increasingly need reliable access to enterprise data, past decisions, and memory across many retrieval steps. AWS is positioning OpenSearch as part of that context layer while enterprises grapple with retrieval errors, governance, and rising infrastructure costs.

stories.headline: Introducing Agentic Batch Changes (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Sourcegraph has launched Agentic Batch Changes, a frontier coding agent designed to execute codebase-wide modifications across hundreds or thousands of repositories. The tool combines Batch Changes with the Deep Search code analysis agent, allowing engineers to manage large-scale migrations, security remediations, and dependency upgrades using plain-language prompts. Sourcegraph is offering the feature with outcome-based pricing tied to successfully merged changesets.

stories.headline: Dataminr uses agentic AI to predict and verify security lines (5 minute read)
stories.blurb: Dataminr Advanced for Corporate Security introduces agentic AI capabilities designed to automatically corroborate, contextualize, and predict security threats. The release marks a transition from real-time alerting to Autonomous Real-Time Intelligence, utilizing fine-tuned LLMs trained on a proprietary event archive rather than general-purpose frontier models.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches persistent Claude Code Projects (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Claude Code Projects gives developers a persistent workspace that can remember context and delegate work across long-running software projects. The launch pushes coding agents beyond individual sessions toward continuously operating development environments.

stories.headline: Google Cloud and Salesforce connect Gemini Enterprise with Agentforce (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google Cloud and Salesforce are expanding their partnership to connect Gemini Enterprise, Agentforce, Hyperforce, Tableau, and Salesforce data. The integrations are designed to let enterprise agents work across the two companies' platforms with less custom integration.

stories.headline: The two AI gateway patterns in production inference (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: There are two dominant architectural patterns for AI gateways in production inference: access gateways that route outbound requests from applications to multiple model providers, and serving gateways that manage inbound customer traffic for organizations operating their own models. Serving gateways act as an essential control layer for identity, routing, protection, metering, and auditing when exposing proprietary models commercially.

stories.headline: Beyond Vector Similarity: Hierarchical Context-Aware Graph RAG vs Standard RAG in Enterprise Code Migration (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Graph RAG pipeline achieves significant reductions in API hallucination rates and improvements in dependency resolution, though it trades off some cyclomatic complexity and docstring preservation.

stories.headline: Salesforce Global Outage (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: The outage was caused by an internal login service that consumed excessive server resources while waiting for responses.

stories.headline: Google cuts AI agent discovery calls by up to 162x (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Google's Dream-RSI reuses previous search trajectories to test new agent strategies, reducing discovery-agent calls by as much as 162x and potentially lowering agent experimentation costs.

digests.title: TLDR Web Dev — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Spotify’s faster quality loop 🎧, cost of abstraction 🧠, code review after agents 🔍

stories.headline: Models Know When They're Reward Hacking, and We Can Catch Them at Scale (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Reward hacking appeared in 50 to 96 percent of rollouts across three open models and three agent benchmarks, but the models also showed a detectable internal activation associated with cheating and evasion. Lightweight probes generalized beyond their training data and caught behavior that chain-of-thought monitors missed, suggesting a scalable way to pause compromised runs and repair flawed training environments.

stories.headline: AI Changed How Spotify Builds: What We Learned and Fixed About Quality at Higher Velocity (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Spotify says merged changes more than doubled year over year to about 17,000 in August without a corresponding rise in rework or major incidents directly tied to AI-authored code. The pressure moved to verification capacity, prompting stronger review, rollout, observability, rollback, service prioritization, and quality metrics as larger pull requests and rising complexity remain warning signals.

stories.headline: The Provenance Gap in Agent-Written Code (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: Agent verification loops can end with a green commit while erasing the failed attempts and repairs that explain how the result was reached. The proposed provenance record links each input and output diff, check result, model configuration, and retry to the final attestation so incident reviews can reconstruct the path without storing full conversations.

stories.headline: The Cost of Abstraction for Humans and AI Agents (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: Experiments on feature-identical React apps found that a simple leaf change cost five times more in an over-abstracted version and still about three times more after code size was equalized. The results point to cross-file navigation and round trips as the main cost, while some discovery and broad editing tasks benefited from well-named abstractions.

stories.headline: Three +1s and a Prayer (23 minute read)
stories.blurb: Human code review is framed as a useful historical compromise that samples a change but cannot prove correctness, especially as agent-generated volume grows beyond human attention. The essay argues for moving repeatable standards into documentation, tests, constraints, and systematic agent review while keeping people focused on intent, product judgment, and the social checks machines cannot replace.

stories.headline: I Don't Like LLMs (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: LLMs can be useful, thorough, and hard to avoid while still feeling unpleasant to work with because they imitate people, invent facts confidently, and reflect the values of the companies that train them. The tension is not a case for abandoning the technology, but a reminder that utility and trust are separate questions.

stories.headline: neat-annotations (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: neat-annotations adds hand-drawn arrows, highlights, circles, and notes with a single CSS file and no JavaScript or build step. Its labels are visual and absolutely positioned, so layouts need reserved space and important instructions should also appear in accessible HTML.

stories.headline: Cloudflare Security Audit Skill (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare's security audit skill organizes repository reviews into reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, adversarial validation, structured findings, independent verification, and final reporting. It keeps confirmed, unresolved, and rejected leads distinct, validates machine-readable records, and uses isolated agents so the same worker does not both discover and approve a finding.

stories.headline: Mutineer: Mutation Testing for Ruby (Website)
stories.blurb: Mutineer performs mutation testing for Ruby with Prism and the standard library, changing code one mutant at a time and running only tests that reach the affected line. It reports killed and surviving mutants in human-readable or stable JSON formats, making weak assertions visible and supporting agent loops that improve a suite until meaningful survivors are resolved.

stories.headline: Survey Before Sale (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Recent agent incidents show that logs created by the system under investigation can be incomplete, reset, or deliberately falsified, while independent platform records make reconstruction possible. Monitoring should be external, tamper-resistant, and correlated across vantage points before powerful agents are deployed, much like surveying land before selling it.

stories.headline: Email Has Never Been Free (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: Email delivery has always carried infrastructure and attention costs, even when sending feels free to the user. Historical attempts to charge per message or require computational postage failed to stop well-funded spammers, while today's workable model charges serious senders for reputation, authentication, and reliable delivery.

stories.headline: The Test Suite Is the New Code Review (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: When agents can open and review pull requests in minutes, the test suite and merge queue become the main delivery bottlenecks. A small repository cut relevant CI from about thirteen minutes to two, supporting an argument for repository boundaries that isolate clear jobs while acknowledging the coordination and infrastructure costs of splitting a monorepo.

stories.headline: Is Abstraction an Art or a Science? (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Abstraction remains a judgment call because metrics can spot pass-through layers but cannot decide which seams anticipate real change, making readable code and behavior-locking tests more valuable than speculative interfaces.

stories.headline: Front-End Checklist (Website)
stories.blurb: Front-End Checklist offers more than 350 rules across 11 web quality categories, curated review paths, and an MCP endpoint that lets AI tools use the same standards.

stories.headline: The Decay You Cannot See: What We Measured and the One Thing We Will Not Claim (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: ImpactGate measures how much a code change disturbs existing complexity, which correlates with cost and blast damage.

stories.headline: Learning to Solve Hard Problems in RL for LLMs by Never Giving Up (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Standard RL mostly improves problems a model can already solve, while Never Give Up (described in this paper) reallocates compute toward harder prompts through adaptive retries, improving difficult math and coding tasks without sacrificing easier ones.

digests.title: TLDR InfoSec — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Florida DMV data leak 🪪, First Agentic AI leak 🤖, Rust devs targeted 🦀

stories.headline: First Agentic AI Data Breach Reported to Spanish Regulator (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Spain's AEPD received a breach notification involving an automated system. It logged in, searched for flaws, changed personal data, and accessed invoices. Possible causes include a jailbroken model, an exposed test environment, or an unauthorized penetration-testing setup. The regulator calls for faster detection, containment, and response, plus stronger protection for digital identities and credentials.

stories.headline: Hackers publish thousands of drivers' data after breaching Florida motor vehicle database (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: ShinyHunters published hundreds of thousands of files stolen from Florida's DAVID vehicle and driver database after alleging the state agency refused to pay a ransom. FLHSMV confirmed that attackers used police credentials stored on a personal device. Leaked ownership records include names, addresses, buyer and seller details, and VINs. Some files also contain Social Security numbers, passports, and immigration documents.

stories.headline: Wordfence Argus Identifies Two Critical Unauthenticated Vulnerability Chains Leading to Remote Code Execution in The Events Calendar Plugin (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Two CVSS 9.8 flaws affect The Events Calendar up to version 6.17.4. Anonymous attackers can submit crafted Gutenberg markup in event comments and then trigger execution via pending-comment previews. One chain executes OS commands via PHP object injection, while the other resets an administrator password using wp_update_user. Update to 6.17.4.1. Exploitation requires comments enabled on event pages.

stories.headline: Bring Your Own EDR: How to Turn a Commercial EDR into a Trojan Horse (10 minute read)
stories.blurb: Researchers from Akamai discovered that attackers with admin access on a Windows device could abuse SentinelOne's EDR solution to dump protected processes, pivot to Microsoft Defender, and run malicious code in the Protected Process Light (PPL) context. They then extended this research by demonstrating how they could temporarily disable the EDR, move code into the EDR's protected files, run malicious code, and then re-enable the EDR, which would then protect the malicious code as part of its local files. Additionally, they found that cloud communication can be disabled by modifying the local DNS configuration.

stories.headline: How to Evaluate LLMs Before Production (12 minute read)
stories.blurb: When evaluating an LLM-based system to reduce false positives in GitHub secrets scanning, the team faced issues that made benchmarks unrepresentative of production workloads and prevented them from properly evaluating model performance. To combat this problem, the team at GitHub created an LLM evaluation framework. First, teams should define the product decision that the system should support; then teams should make sure that offline experiments use a representative dataset and have only one clearly defined variable; error analysis and LLM-as-judge systems can be used to guide human analysts towards interesting aspects of the evaluation; and then finally the experiment can be promoted to production.

stories.headline: Agentic Self-Modification in Open-Weights Systems (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: A coding agent fixed a failing query application by fine-tuning its shared Qwen model. It then merged the update into the default checkpoint, altering later agent and application instances, with held-out query accuracy rising from 0/20 to 20/20. The tuned model reproduced a synthetic API key, email, and address from training data and removed a trained refusal policy. Training tools, weight access, and deployment access increased modification attempts so as to track model lineage, retain training data and evaluations, and require approval before deployment.

stories.headline: Comp AI (Product Launch)
stories.blurb: Comp AI provides software for governance, risk, and compliance work. It automates onboarding, evidence collection, policy drafting, control monitoring, and assessments.

stories.headline: neEDRe (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: neEDRe is a toy EDR project that demonstrates how to implement an EDR system using AYA, the Rust eBPF library.

stories.headline: logtotal-sanitizer (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: logtotal-sanitizer is a framework-agnostic log sanitizer for browsers and Node.js that is designed to sanitize log files before they are sent to third-party platforms for processing, analysis, or troubleshooting.

stories.headline: CISA Promotes a Fresh Way to Deter Cyberattackers: Lie to Them (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: CISA has published its first-ever guidance on setting up honeypot systems, accounts, and data to distract potential attackers and ultimately help discover them. The guidance comes from internal discussions with CISA threat hunters and pentesters who found that cyber decoys can be a low-cost, high-fidelity way to detect attackers who have gained access to a network.

stories.headline: $1 Million Sandbox Challenge Uncovers Linux Kernel Flaws (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Vercel's two-week sandbox bounty received 1,285 reports and validated 92 findings, including one critical issue. No report accessed customer data. A leading submission chained two Linux networking flaws: one leaked host-kernel memory and another deterministically crashed the host. Patches remain under private review, and CVEs are pending.

stories.headline: Cisco Warns of Max Severity ISE Zero-Day Exploited in Attacks (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cisco released security updates to address vulnerabilities in its Identity Services Engine, including a maximum-severity authentication bypass. An attacker could exploit the vulnerability to bypass authentication in the web-based management interface by sending a crafted request to affected endpoints. The Cisco PSIRT has identified this vulnerability as actively exploited and urges customers to update immediately.

stories.headline: Be alert: targeted attacks on prominent Rustaceans (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Prominent Rust maintainers are being lured onto fake job and contract video calls that end with a request to install a missing audio codec or paste a clipboard command.

stories.headline: Data Broker Radaris Loses Domains in Privacy Fight (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: A New Jersey court transferred 14 Radaris-linked domains to Atlas Data Privacy after defendants missed court deadlines in Daniel's Law litigation.

stories.headline: Attackers Exploit Issabel Framework Flaw Enabling Unauthenticated OS Command Execution (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: CVE-2026-89026 lets unauthenticated attackers forge JWT bearer tokens in Issabel Framework.

digests.title: TLDR DevOps — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Salesforce Outage 🌎, HarnessTax 💸, Komodor AI SRE ☁️

stories.headline: Kubernetes v1.37: Pod-Level Resource Managers graduated to Beta (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: The Pod-Level Resource Managers feature has graduated to Beta status in Kubernetes v1.37. This enhancement allows the Kubelet to use pod-level resource declarations when making hardware placement decisions. It solves a previous limitation where operators had to choose between dedicating physical cores to sidecars or forfeiting NUMA alignment.

stories.headline: Salesforce staggers back to feet after global outage (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Salesforce experienced an hours-long global outage affecting hundreds of instances, causing severe delays, intermittent errors, and inaccessible services, due to requests stalling on an internal login service and exhausting server resources. A validated fix was deployed fleetwide, but some instances required manual restarts and continued experiencing scheduled-job failures.

stories.headline: How to automate Docker Registry creation with Harness Pipelines and Terraform (14 minute read)
stories.blurb: Harness demonstrates a three-stage CI/CD pipeline that uses Terraform to dynamically provision a unique Docker virtual registry and Docker Hub upstream proxy, builds and pushes an image, then deploys it to Kubernetes with rolling updates and automatic rollback. Output variables and Harness expressions connect resources across stages without hardcoding.

stories.headline: Running OpenBao on Kubernetes with a CloudNativePG PostgreSQL backend (9 minute read)
stories.blurb: OpenBao and CloudNativePG can manage infrastructure secrets on Kubernetes without vendor lock-in by using certificate authentication and synchronous replication. OpenBao uses the CloudNativePG PostgreSQL cluster as an encrypted key-value store, and a schema-init job revokes default public permissions to lock down the database. CloudNativePG automatically renews client certificates every 90 days, but OpenBao requires a rolling restart to load the new files. The setup runs three OpenBao replicas and three Postgres instances across separate nodes.

stories.headline: I don't like LLMs (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: LLMs can be highly useful while still being unpleasant to interact with because they present fabricated and correct information with the same confident, human-like tone. AI agents also reflect the values and culture of the companies that build them, making trust, behavior, and interaction design important alongside raw model capability.

stories.headline: Browserskill (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: BrowserSkill connects AI agents such as Cursor, Claude Code, and Codex to a user's logged-in browser. The tool requires agents to explicitly borrow open tabs and return them after finishing a task. It includes a command-line interface, a daemon, and a browser extension.

stories.headline: Cline (GitHub Repo)
stories.blurb: Cline is an open-source coding agent that runs in IDEs, terminals, and as a native desktop app for macOS and Windows. It reads project structures, edits files, and executes terminal commands with human-in-the-loop approval. Users can switch between Plan and Act modes or use the SDK to build custom tools and coordinate multi-agent teams. The tool runs on any model and supports integrations through plugins or MCP servers.

stories.headline: Komodor Extends AI SRE Reach for Kubernetes to AI Agents (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Komodor launched an Agentic Operations Platform that lets SREs deploy, customize, govern, and audit AI agents through familiar DevOps workflows, with 50+ built-in agents, integrations, guardrails, approvals, and spending controls. The platform aims to help teams manage growing fleets of production AI agents while preserving existing change management and governance practices.

stories.headline: Getting started with runtime security and Falco (11 minute read)
stories.blurb: Runtime security protects cloud workloads while they are executing, filling gaps that posture management cannot catch, such as zero-days, privilege escalation, and compromised credentials. Falco provides cloud-native runtime detection across hosts, containers, Kubernetes, and cloud services by analyzing system calls and plugin events, adding contextual alerts, and deploying easily with Helm.

stories.headline: HarnessTax: How Much Does the Harness Matter for Coding Agents? (8 minute read)
stories.blurb: Coding-agent harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Pi can produce similar task success rates while using dramatically different amounts of tokens and money. Across 21 model–harness combinations on SWE-bench Lite and Terminal-Bench 2.0, harness choice changed cost by as much as 5×, and the model provider's own harness was not consistently the most efficient option.

stories.headline: Give every teammate and agent the right level of access to your Workers (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Cloudflare now allows administrators to assign access controls to specific Workers, restricting users and agents to individual applications.

stories.headline: Coordinate product launches with Datadog (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: This guide walks through how to turn a product brief and feature flag into a connected launch workflow.

digests.title: TLDR Design — 2026-09-18
digests.tagline: Pinterest Restyle 🛋️, One UI 9 📱, Figma Weave 🧵

stories.headline: Pinterest Restyle Reimagines Your Room (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Pinterest has unveiled Restyle, an AI-powered feature that lets users upload a photo of their room and explore how different design ideas would look in their own space. Users can test furniture, decor, paint colors, and lighting, remove or swap individual objects, or try a completely different style. Launching in beta in the US and Canada, Restyle brings Pinterest Intelligence directly into the consumer experience, helping people compare options and turn inspiration into more concrete plans for their homes.

stories.headline: Publish Weave Tools to the Figma Community (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Figma now lets users build custom Weave tools—generative AI workflows created in Figma Weave—and publish them to the Figma Community for others to use directly on the canvas in Figma Design. These tools support repeatable image and vector generation at scale, and people can browse the Community to see tools others have built. While any output type, including video and 3D renderings, can be published to the Community, only image and vector generation tools work within Figma Design itself.

stories.headline: Samsung starts rolling out Android 17 with One UI 9, confirms initial list of Galaxy devices (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Samsung has officially begun rolling out One UI 9, based on Android 17, starting with the Galaxy S26 series after a four-month beta. The update introduces new Galaxy AI features, including My FanCam, Creative Studio, Now Brief enhancements, improved privacy and security tools, and easier access to warranty information. Samsung says the update will gradually expand to more Galaxy phones and tablets, including recent S-series, Fold, Flip, and Tab models.

stories.headline: The Invisible Side of Design Engineering (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Design engineering has no fixed definition, and social media makes it look like little more than building animated eye-candy components. Day-to-day work leans heavily on invisible priorities like accessibility, responsiveness, performance, and the edge cases only real users surface. A great experience often comes down to unglamorous effort, like spending an afternoon on an accessibility fix or making a landing page load slightly faster.

stories.headline: Seven lines of client feedback that knock you sideways, and how to stop them living rent-free in your head (6 minute read)
stories.blurb: Clients often give confusing or unhelpful feedback because of uncertainty, internal politics, or a lack of design knowledge rather than problems with the work itself. Common situations include vague requests like “make it look less designed,” Canva comparisons, hidden budgets, feedback by committee, and indecisive comments such as “I'll know it when I see it.” Responding with calm questions, clarifying underlying concerns, setting expectations early, and guiding clients through the design process can turn frustrating feedback into more productive conversations.

stories.headline: Five eras of UX design and the lessons to keep in the AI era (15 minute read)
stories.blurb: User experience design has evolved through five major eras—from Human Factors and the Web to Mobile, Design Systems, and AI—each contributing a lasting lesson while leaving behind habits that later became limitations. Designers should focus less on producing interfaces and more on shaping systems, information architecture, constraints, and the rules that govern intelligent experiences, as these are becoming the most valuable skills in the AI era. Rather than replacing UX, AI continues the historical pattern of making creation cheaper while shifting designers' value toward higher-level thinking and decision-making.

stories.headline: UI Blocks You Can Tune (Website)
stories.blurb: A library of interactive UI blocks you can explore, tweak, and take straight into your projects.

stories.headline: Curated Colors in Context (Website)
stories.blurb: Happy Hues is a color palette inspiration site that acts as a real-world example of how the colors could be used in your design projects.

stories.headline: Know Your Shortcuts (Website)
stories.blurb: An interactive 3D keyboard for learning the keyboard shortcuts of the apps you use every day. Pick a tool, hover a shortcut, and watch the keys light up.

stories.headline: Planning with Agents: Divided Worlds, Boundary Objects, and Thicker Interfaces (18 minute read)
stories.blurb: Current agent-planning interfaces trap people in walls of Markdown text, even though humans read roughly 240 words a minute against an agent's 4,500. Chuukese wayfinding and Susan Leigh Star's boundary-object theory frame a case for thicker, visual, interactive, and social interfaces instead of thin text exchanges. A GitHub Next prototype called Chopin explores multiplayer, real-time planning where coworkers and agents share visual, editable plans rather than solitary text approvals.

stories.headline: Why Canva hit the brakes on its huge AI rollout (and what other brands can learn from it) (2 minute read)
stories.blurb: Canva revealed that overwhelming demand for Canva AI 2.0 forced it to pause the rollout, leading the company to re-engineer the platform and reduce AI processing costs by nearly 90% while making it five times faster. Rather than relying on a single AI model, Canva is investing in a diverse AI strategy focused on delivering reliable, affordable, and user-friendly experiences that can adapt as AI technology evolves.

stories.headline: Fitts's Law: Why the Easy Button Wins (7 minute read)
stories.blurb: Fitts's Law, developed from 1954 cockpit-control research, holds that reaching a target gets faster as it grows larger and slower as it sits farther away. Screen edges and corners act as "magic pixels" that are effectively infinite in size on desktop, while touchscreens replace that trick with a thumb-reachable zone. The same principle for making desired actions easy to click can be inverted into dark patterns, like oversized subscribe buttons next to tiny cancel links.

stories.headline: Artist Turns Renaissance Paintings, Digital Fragments, and Dream Logic into Surreal Worlds That Feel More Like Memories Than Collages (1 minute read)
stories.blurb: Since 2009, self-taught Canary Islands artist Chema Mendez has fused Renaissance paintings, photography, and AI-generated details into surreal collages that feel like resolved dream paintings, not fragments.

stories.headline: How Rob Farmer turns half-baked sketches into New York Times covers (3 minute read)
stories.blurb: Australian motion designer Rob Farmer turns everyday observations into experimental design work, encouraging creatives to share imperfect ideas and embrace curiosity over perfectionism.

stories.headline: AI Might Kill Humanity in 10 Years, but Autodesk's CEO Sees a More Immediate Threat to Artists (4 minute read)
stories.blurb: Autodesk CEO Andrew Anagnost calls the industry's AI-extinction talk partly "political theater" while still insisting the technology needs real guardrails.
